title: Exact sequence inverse image preserves K-flatness
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and schemes in a universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme]. For a scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose index $n\geq0$ means $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$, with actual quotient ring maps; put $A_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be its category of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-semilinear systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $e_{W,n}$ for exact evaluation, $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $A_W\to B_{W,n}$ and $U_W:\mathscr S_W\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ for their simultaneous exact scalar restriction. Use ordinary unbounded integer-indexed cochain and derived categories, with localization $q_W$ for $A_W$-modules, $q^s_W$ for sequence modules and $q^t_W$ for towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, with $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ D(U_W)$, and the specified derived tensor and cochain tensor models on the sequence site [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A good integral complex is K-flat with flat terms; K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic module complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All comparisons below use the actual chosen adjunctions, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their objects. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness of inputs, or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes is assumed. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, let $b_f$ on sequence sites be $(n,V)\mapsto(n,X\times_Y V)$. Its ring map is the actual constant-section coefficient map at every $n$; let $f^s_*:\mathscr S_X\to\mathscr S_Y$ be its module direct image, $F_f:\mathscr S_Y\to\mathscr S_X$ its specified left adjoint, $\eta^f$ the unit, and $D_f=D(F_f)$ the exact induced derived inverse image [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Finite module pullback $f_n^*$ is equipped with its actual adjunction unit. The direct-image/evaluation comparison is identity on sections; the fixed inverse-image/evaluation isomorphism $v_{f,n}:f_n^* e_{Y,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{X,n}F_f$ is its inverse mate under the specified finite and sequence adjunctions. If $P$ is any K-flat coherent sequence complex on $Y$, then $F_f^cP$ is K-flat on $X$. Explicitly, K-flatness means that $\operatorname{Tot}(Z\otimes P)$ is acyclic for every acyclic sequence-module complex $Z$ on $Y$, and the conclusion is that $\operatorname{Tot}(Z'\otimes F_f^cP)$ is acyclic for every acyclic sequence-module complex $Z'$ on $X$. These are the IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients predicates at the actual sequence-site universes (objects $u+1$, morphisms $u$, modules $u+1$). No termwise-flatness assumption is made on $P$; no boundedness, normalized-system, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is made. This is pullbackTensorSequenceGood for the actual exact inverse image along the canonical constant-section ring map.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat) only covers flat-term representatives; Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product). The stated extension to arbitrary K-flat complexes for the exact constant-coefficient sequence pullback is a project obligation, not a quotation of 0G7E.

proof.text: Use coefficientTensorModelPreservation.2 to obtain K-flatness of every finite evaluation of P. For an arbitrary acyclic sequence complex Z, its evaluations are acyclic by exactness of coefficientSequenceEvaluation. The cochain tensor evaluation isomorphism identifies each evaluation of Tot(Z tensor C) with the finite total tensor. Componentwise exactness of semilinear systems therefore detects K-flatness of C from that of every evaluation.
Apply completedTowerFinitePullbackKFlat to each finite evaluation of P, which is K-flat by Step 1. It applies to the actual integralOperationsLevelPullback, without any flat-term hypothesis.

The specified inverse-image/evaluation complex comparison identifies each evaluation of the actual sequence pullback with the finite pullback of the source evaluation. Transport K-flatness through this cochain isomorphism and apply the componentwise criterion of Step 1.
